Senses.PreferredTarget: Complete Command of the Precious Mirror
Senses.Explanation: The four graphs literally name the precious mirror (寶鏡) and complete command (三昧). In the Chan record this is not a generic state: it is the title and transmitted Caodong text associated with Dongshan Liangjie. Dongshan tells Caoshan that he personally received the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror from his former teacher Yunyan, that its matter exhausts the essential point, and that he now entrusts it to Caoshan (吾在雲巖先師處親印寶鏡三昧，事窮的要，今付于汝). A later commentary consequently calls it a book transmitted privately by Dongshan to Caoshan (寶鏡三昧一書，洞山室中密授曹山者也). The text itself opens, “This such thing was secretly entrusted by buddhas and ancestors; you have now obtained it, so guard it well” (如是之法，佛祖密付；汝今得之，宜善保護), then gives the paired images “a silver bowl filled with snow; the bright moon hiding a heron” (銀盌盛雪，明月藏鷺) and says that although their kinds are not the same, mixed together their places are known (類之弗齊，混則知處). Across later Caodong records its title is joined to the Five Ranks, upright and crooked, ruler and minister, and the paired wording “he is not me; I am precisely he” (渠不是我，我正是渠). A direct question, “What is the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror?” receives, “Do not reflect idle light and shadows; return his old face” (不照閒光影，還他舊面皮). These are the transmitted title, contents, relations, and recorded answer; the corpus supplies no single prose substitution for the whole text.
Senses.Note: #0g deviation: the phrase is deployed as the proper name of a Caodong transmission text and house inheritance, not merely as the ordinary image of a valuable mirror or the standalone word for complete command. Attribution of authorship is not fully uniform: Dongshan's record says he received it from Yunyan and entrusted it to Caoshan; later records also call it Dongshan's text or report older attributions. The entry therefore reports the transmission claims without deciding authorship. Allowlisted count: 117 hits in 49 texts; the title form “Song of the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror” (寶鏡三昧歌) occurs 3 times in one text.

Occurrences.Kwic: 吾在雲巖先師處親印寶鏡三昧。事窮的要。今付于汝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Dongshan tells Caoshan: “I personally received the Complete Command of the Precious Mirror from my former teacher Yunyan. Its matter exhausts the essential point. I now entrust it to you.”

Occurrences.Kwic: 寶鏡三昧一書，洞山室中密授曹山者也。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Extensive Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄), Yongjue Yuanxian's commentary on the Precious Mirror Complete Command (寶鏡三昧註). Yongjue Yuanxian identifies it as the book privately transmitted by Dongshan Liangjie to Caoshan Benji; Dongshan and Caoshan are persons discussed, not the expository speaker.

Occurrences.Kwic: 洞山价禪師寶鏡三昧如是之法，佛祖密付。汝今得之，宜善保護。銀盌盛雪，明月藏鷺。類之弗齊，混則知處。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The titled text's opening and its paired precious-mirror images: silver bowl and snow, moon and heron.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧：「如何是寶鏡三昧？」師：「不照閒光影，還他舊面皮。」
Occurrences.AttributionNote: 雪關禪師語錄, concise public exchange. The exact headword-bearing speaker is an unnamed questioning monk: he asks what the precious-mirror samadhi is, and Xueguan Zhiyin answers that it does not reflect idle lights and shadows but returns the old face. The six-rung review found no personal name for this monk.
